title: Substance and medical rule-outs
about: Questions on substances, medications and medical conditions that can mimic or worsen anxiety, panic and low mood (for example caffeine, thyroid problems, heart rhythm problems), and on new confusion or cognitive decline that calls for medical or cognitive evaluation. Substance answers stay in this session's memory only (42 CFR Part 2).

questions.text: Could caffeine or energy drinks, alcohol, cannabis or other drugs, or a medication started, stopped or changed recently explain some of these symptoms?
questions.why: Caffeine, stimulants, decongestants, cannabis, alcohol and withdrawal from alcohol or sedatives can produce panic, anxiety, low mood and poor sleep. Medication changes can too. Ask before attributing symptoms to a mental health pattern.

options.label: Caffeine or energy drinks could explain them
Cannabis or other drugs could explain them
A medication started, stopped or changed could explain them
options.note: Review with the prescriber; do not suggest stopping a medication without them.

options.label: None of these seems to explain them

questions.text: Has a medical check looked for physical causes that can mimic these symptoms, such as an overactive thyroid, heart rhythm problems, low blood sugar, asthma or medication side effects?
questions.why: Several medical problems produce racing heart, breathlessness, shaking or dizziness. Ruling them out protects the client and makes the anxiety work more credible to them.

options.label: A medical cause is suspected or known
Not checked yet
options.note: Suggest a primary care review, especially with chest pain, fainting, or symptoms that are new or changing.

questions.text: Has a medical check looked for physical causes of low mood and tiredness, such as an underactive thyroid, anemia, low vitamin levels, sleep apnea or medication side effects?
questions.why: Thyroid problems, anemia, vitamin deficiencies, sleep apnea and some medications can cause or deepen low mood and fatigue. A recent check makes the rest of the picture easier to read.

options.label: A medical cause is suspected or known
Not checked yet
options.note: Suggest a primary care review, including basic blood tests where appropriate.

questions.text: Is there new confusion, drowsiness or attention that comes and goes over hours or days, or a gradual decline in memory, thinking or everyday tasks over months?
questions.why: Sudden or fluctuating confusion suggests delirium, which needs same-day medical care (NICE CG103). A gradual decline suggests a neurocognitive disorder that needs a cognitive evaluation (NICE NG97). Either can look like depression, anxiety, mania or psychosis.

options.label: Sudden or fluctuating confusion over hours or days
options.note: Possible delirium: arrange a same-day medical assessment. This is a referral, not a finding.

options.label: A gradual decline in memory, thinking or daily tasks over months
options.note: Refer for a cognitive evaluation through primary care or a memory service.
